definition: Dynamometry is a method of measuring strength with specialized equipment. In the supplied source, isokinetic dynamometry is described as a commonly used way to assess hamstring strength for monitoring reliability, fatigue-related changes, and differences between limbs.

reasons: The packet does not explicitly define “dynamometry” as “a method of measuring strength with specialized equipment,” so the first substantive claim of the definition is unsupported.

The packet supports only that isokinetic dynamometry was the most frequently used hamstring-strength assessment modality; it does not define dynamometry in general as a method of measuring strength with specialized equipment.

The second sentence overstates the source by saying it is used for monitoring reliability, fatigue-related changes, and limb differences; the article reports reliability, post-activity fatigue sensitivity, and inter-limb asymmetry patterns, but not that these are the specific purposes of isokinetic dynamometry.
The definition narrows the term to a specific application in hamstring assessment without showing that this is the requested general sense of 'dynamometry'.
